## Repair 1 — the commissioned cause

`execFileSync('readlink',['-f','/proc/self/fd/9'])` resolved `/proc/self` inside the **spawned readlink**. Measured in a real held child:

| reader | observed |
|---|---|
| in-process `fs.readlinkSync` | `/tmp/finale-window-fdcheck-….lock` ✅ |
| old spawned `readlink -f` | `/proc/<readlink-pid>/fd/9` |

The old reader **didn't even error** — it returned the readlink process's own `/proc` path, which can never equal the lock path, so `owned` was *always false*.

Fixed with in-process `readlinkSync` + `fstatSync`/`statSync` **dev+inode** matching. Kernel exclusive `FLOCK WRITE` retained. Contention now accepts **only flock exit 1**; spawn errors/signals/other statuses are `conclusive:false` and refused.

**7/7 cases against the ACTUAL exported `verifyHeavyLock` in real Node children** with inherited exclusive fd 9 on a unique temp lock: held-pass (contention exit 1), missing-fd, wrong-fd-pipe, wrong-target, unheld-refusal, two arg guards. Case A could not have passed under the old code. Transport reused from the existing `fd-transport-diagnostic.mjs`.

Three retained failed attempts were faults in **my harness**, not the probe (fd 8 = capture pipe, fd 21 = `/dev/null`, `exec 21>&-` reopened by Node) — the probe correctly refused each time. Fixed by having the child pick a descriptor it has *proven* closed instead of guessing.

## Repair 2 — new fault, reachable only because Repair 1 worked

The run reached a real browser for the first time in this lane, then crashed on `install.inventory`. Proven on shipped headed Chrome: **playwright-core evaluates a string pageFunction as an expression and ignores the second argument** — `(cfg) => {…}` serialised to `undefined` and **the installer never ran** (`window.__marker` stayed null; the invoked form returned the object). Fixed by invoking the expression with the config inlined; `buildInstallerSource` unchanged. Root's control note independently authorizes this exact correction.

Therefore `no-stream-on-owned-sink` was a **consequence of the probe crashing before the game made sound** — not evidence about game audio.
